- Role/lifetime boundary: 82 Gateway tests and 19 bridge tests passed against this source, including actual-router/SQLite coverage for scoped and inherited restricted operators, unknown synthetic denial, mixed-actor deferred cleanup, expired foreground callers, patch/patchMany/assignOwner, group commits, and reset. The separate agent-owned reset finish-after-lifecycle-rotation contract remains green. The final independent Codex P0–P2 review found no actionable defects.
- Runtime batch proof: the built dashboard restored the archived fixture with its current session ID, applied exactly one two-target patch, and re-listed both persisted rows as active, unpinned, and in Verified. The result was `succeeded: [0, 1]`, `failed: []`. The captured tool sequence contains only session tools. Lifecycle/replacement tests (7) and single/batch session-tool tests (61) also passed. The dashboard fixture uses an authorized admin; restricted-role and post-closure rejection are proven at the actual Gateway router/storage boundary, not inferred from the screenshots.
- Production growth: +159 lines provide generalized bounded patch input/results, +140 enforce caller identity/lifetime and explicit cleanup transfer at existing owners, and +5 clarify the shell tool label. Parsing is shared and mutation ownership remains canonical. This is the owner-reviewed scope requested by the maintainer; no parallel mutator was added.
- Data-model classification: `sessions-tool-patch.ts` serializes bounded model-visible tool results; it does not store them in a new persistence format. No SQLite schema, migration, schema version, stored representation, configuration option, or Gateway protocol changed. The existing state was created before the final build, then reopened and successfully restored/patched by the final build. No data migration is required.

These address the listed verification, growth, and compatibility requests. The fresh review has no code/security finding; the pending CI run is the remaining landing gate. No source changes followed the review.

Both lifecycle findings and rank-up moves are addressed in the current head, `53a5dc41bec`.

- Group rename/delete now retain the source catalog and sidebar while guarded member writes complete. Interrupted work stays discoverable and retryable, concurrent catalog edits are preserved, and clients refresh even on failure. The regressions assert catalog/member coherence across both agent stores, interruption before and after partial progress, retry, destination removal, late members, and concurrent source edits. The focused group/handler/router set passed 48 tests. A live Gateway and open dashboard also verified rename/delete across two agent stores, reopening state created by the earlier build.
- Reset now hands completion of an existing lifecycle to the reset owner immediately before destructive cleanup. Normal rotation and incognito deletion finish after caller closure; exact identity, lifecycle revision and SQLite compare-and-swap preserve replacements. Missing-row creation still checks live authority through commit. The actual built-in bridge → Gateway handler → reset owner reproduced both failures before the fix. The 30-test reset cleanup/concurrency set passed, followed by the final 8-test concurrency rerun after fixture type cleanup. The reset correction is net-neutral in production lines.

The branch is rebased onto `dc73b1aa54eb`. That comparison found an interaction with the new owner-attribution authority field; cleanup now preserves the effective foreground actor. Both new regressions failed before the fix, and all 44 authority/router tests passed. Independent Codex reviews of the group, integration, and reset corrections are clean; production and exact affected test types, typed lint, and formatting passed.

There is no SQLite schema, stored representation, configuration, migration or protocol change. `sessions-tool-patch.ts` serializes bounded model-visible tool results; it is not a persistence format. Existing-state reopening was verified by the live group run. Final-head CI and the final supported build/live reset check are running; their results will be recorded before landing.

Final-head validation is complete at `04c6984443b76cc5e895ab0fb522c6f7455057cf`.

The full supported build and live dedicated-tool flow passed through `/tools/invoke`: cross-agent inventory, one two-target patch, persisted group/pin verification, archive, restore, and final verification. The batch returned `succeeded: [0, 1]`, `failed: []`, `errors: []`. The same built Gateway passed two-agent group rename/delete, normal reset, and incognito deletion.

The 44 authority/router tests, 22 background-runtime tests, production types, exact core test-type stripe 3/5, scoped typed lint, formatting, and independent Codex review pass. The original actor defect and the group/reset caller-expiry races each have red-to-green owner-boundary regressions. The follow-up integration uses main's canonical AbortSignal and its cross-agent default; no compatibility path was added.

No SQLite schema, stored representation, configuration or protocol changed. Existing-state reopening passed; the JSON identified by the data-model heuristic is a bounded tool result. Final production delta is +304, justified by bounded batch input/results, authority/lifetime handling and coherent group mutations; the reset correction itself is net-neutral.

[Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/33723446737) passed at `04c6984443b76cc5e895ab0fb522c6f7455057cf` (attempt 2), including all selected Node, Gateway/agent, Windows, macOS Swift, Android, and iOS lanes. [Workflow Sanity](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/33723446728) also passed. The only retry in the passing run was Windows checkout after a runner PermissionError, before tests started. A parallel hosted recovery passed Windows but hit the native startup watchdog recorded in the PR follow-ups; its remaining duplicate iPad capture was cancelled after the original iPad capture passed. No source or global CI settings were changed for these runner recoveries. The latest ClawSweeper rank-up request for completed exact-head validation is satisfied.

Merged via squash.
